items.title: Joe Wilder Part 2 interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 12, 1998
items.q: And while we were there it was Ernie Royal, Joe Newman and I were the trumpets.

ctx.x: You know I was so thrilled in a way and surprised too that I ended up for instance in Les Hite’s band because I was 19 years old and this was quite an experience for me, and I remember when I left Philadelphia on a bus to go to Lansing, Michigan to join Les Hite’s band and my mother accompanied me to the bus terminal, and I can remember my mother standing, as I had the window down and the bus is loaded with people, and my mother saying, “don’t you do anything to embarrass this family while you’re away.” And I…

rather surprised and I was actually in awe of most of the fellows who were in those bands. They were a little older than me. Some of them were in my age group but a lot of them were older and had a lot more experience. So I felt kind of lucky to be there. When I left Les Hite I joined the Lionel Hampton band, which at that time was roaring, and I was really in awe of that band. I mean I was again quite happy that I became a member. But it’s strange because the first trumpet player was Carl George and he was…
It wasn’t the easiest gig in the world, from what I understand.

items.title: Joe Wilder — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: So it was Karl George, Ernie Royal, Joe Newman, and me. We were the four trumpets in the band.

ctx.x: Lionel Hampton’s band, they were looking for someone to come into the band temporarily. The first trumpet player was Karl George. He was having – he was in the midst of getting a divorce in St. Louis. He had to go to St. Louis to take care of that. That was going to take two or three weeks, and they needed someone to replace him at that time. So I came. He was still there. He helped me with some of the things in the book. Then he left, and they decided that they would still – instead of replacing him, they would…
years and came back and went back with Lionel Hampton. I stayed only a short time. Then I left them and joined Jimmie Lunceford’s band.

items.title: Joe Wilder Part 1 interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 12, 1996
items.q: You know Joe sat here, I sat here and the drums are there.

ctx.x: Did you get a lot of his solos?

I did some, yes, I had some too. Yeah. It was interesting you know, it was interesting. I was telling that story this morning, about after having joined the band I was there a couple of weeks, a few weeks, and I hadn’t played any solos. And I was getting a little frustrated. So I wrote a little note to Count Basie and I said “Bas, could I play a couple of choruses of just about anything?” And I signed it “the trumpet player second from the drums.” You know Joe sat here, I sat here and the drums are there. And I…
Yeah. The new guy in the band, you know, oh my. What’s the — I read something, I think it may have been with Hampton, about the Barracuda?
